key_insight: FrontierPhysics moves AI evaluation beyond isolated physics questions toward end-to-end research. Its 56 tasks, created by 42 physicists from their own research, are designed to assess research quality alongside correctness.
problem_solved: Existing physics benchmarks focus on fixed questions, isolated subtasks, or reproducing papers with known solutions, leaving agents’ broader research abilities underexamined.
method: Build 56 research-grounded tasks contributed by 42 physicists.
Cover nine domains spanning theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.
Evaluate end-to-end research rather than isolated answers, with attention to both correctness and research quality; detailed procedures are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, FrontierPhysics offers a more research-oriented way to assess physics agents than conventional question-answering tests. The provided abstract does not report performance results.
visual_elements: Metric tiles highlighting 56 tasks, 42 physicists, and nine domains.
Three connected icons representing theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.
Comparison diagram contrasting isolated benchmark questions with end-to-end research tasks.
Two-axis evaluation graphic highlighting correctness and research quality.
paper_title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
paper_authors: Bingran You, Wenjun Ke, Ria Rosenauer, Bo Liu, Wenbo Chen
